title: Weak equivalences form an accessible arrow subcategory
statement: Let $\mathcal M$ be a model category with the conventions of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization]; no simplicial enrichment is required here. A category is locally presentable if it is cocomplete and, for some infinite regular cardinal $\kappa$, generated under small $\kappa$-filtered colimits by a small set of objects $P$ such that $\operatorname{Hom}(P,-)$ preserves these colimits. Here $\kappa$-filtered means every diagram with fewer than $\kappa$ morphisms admits a cocone, and regular means a union of fewer than $\kappa$ sets of cardinality less than $\kappa$ has cardinality less than $\kappa$. Suppose $\mathcal M$ is combinatorial: its underlying category is locally presentable and each of its two weak factorization systems is generated by a small set of arrows, meaning the right class is precisely the maps admitting diagonal fillers against that set. Let $W\subseteq\mathcal M^{[1]}$ be the full subcategory on weak equivalences, with commuting squares as morphisms. A replete full subcategory $\mathcal V\subseteq\mathcal D$ is an accessible subcategory if, for some infinite regular $\lambda$, it is closed under small $\lambda$-filtered colimits computed in $\mathcal D$ and is generated under those colimits by a small set of its objects. Replete means closed under isomorphism in $\mathcal D$. Then $W$ is an accessible subcategory of $\mathcal M^{[1]}$. In particular this includes closure under sufficiently filtered colimits in the ambient arrow category, not just abstract accessibility of $W$.

source.place: Corollary A.2.6.8 (Smith), printed pp. 820-821 (PDF pp. 837-838), weak-equivalence clause only; accessible subcategory is Definition A.2.6.2. No Stacks tag states this model-category accessibility theorem. Read online; not archived in literature/.

proof.text: Write $C,F,W$ for the model classes. Choose small sets $I,J$ with $I^{\square}=F\cap W$ and $J^{\square}=F$, as assumed in the statement. The model-category convention of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization] supplies pullbacks and all small colimits. Apply the presheaf clause of [lem-coef-presheaf-local-presentability] with the small category $[1]^{\mathrm{op}}$ and target $\mathcal M$. Its functor category is $\mathcal M^{[1]}$, so the ambient arrow category is locally presentable. Source and target identify arrow diagrams with pairs of diagrams and a natural map; their pointwise colimit is the arrow colimit because a square out of it is uniquely a pair of compatible maps out of the two endpoint colimits.

source.place: Corollary A.2.6.8 setup; ordinary functor-category local presentability is the cited existing Mathlib leaf.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-small-right-lifting-accessibility] to $\mathcal M$ and the small set $I$. This gives a replete accessible full subcategory $\mathcal R\subseteq\mathcal M^{[1]}$ whose objects are precisely $I^{\square}$. The generating hypothesis identifies $\mathcal R$ with the trivial fibrations $F\cap W$. This input is a theorem about a small lifting class in any locally presentable category; no weak-equivalence accessibility is assumed.

source.place: Corollary A.2.6.8 proof, first two paragraphs, applied only to the generating cofibrations I.

proof.text: Use [lem-coef-accessible-small-object-factorization] for the small set $J$ to obtain $f=p_f i_f$, with middle-object functor $E$, $p_f\in J^{\square}=F$, and $i_f$ in the weak saturation of $J$. To check that $i_f$ is a trivial cofibration, use the weak factorization system $(C\cap W,F)$ of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization], which gives $C\cap W={}^{\square}F$. Every $j\in J$ lies in this left class by the definition of $J^{\square}=F$. The left class is closed under retracts and pushouts by [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure] and under small continuous transfinite compositions by [lem-coef-transfinite-left-lifting]. It contains every isomorphism: a square with invertible left side $j$ has filler $uj^{-1}$. Thus it contains the weak saturation of $J$, and $i_f\in C\cap W$ for every $f$.

source.place: Corollary A.2.6.8 proof, third paragraph, Proposition A.1.2.5; verification that the chosen first factor is a trivial cofibration.

proof.text: Define $T:\mathcal M^{[1]}\to\mathcal M^{[1]}$ by $T(f)=p_f:E(f)\to\operatorname{target}(f)$ and $T(a,b)=(E(a,b),b)$. The equation $p_g E(a,b)=bp_f$ and the identity/composition clauses in [lem-coef-accessible-small-object-factorization] show that this is a functor. That node also gives an infinite regular $\kappa$ for which $E$ preserves small $\kappa$-filtered colimits. Since the other endpoint of $T$ is the target projection and arrow colimits are componentwise by Step 1, $T$ preserves those colimits: the source comparison is the invertible comparison for $E$, the target comparison is the identity, and their square commutes by naturality of $p$.

source.place: Corollary A.2.6.8 proof, third paragraph: the second-factor functor T double-prime preserves sufficiently filtered colimits.

proof.text: For every $f=p_f i_f$, Step 3 gives $i_f\in W$. Two-out-of-three, part of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization], therefore gives $f\in W$ if and only if $p_f\in W$. Since $p_f\in F$, this is equivalent to $T(f)\in\mathcal R$. Hence the full arrow subcategory on weak equivalences is exactly $T^{-1}\mathcal R$. Apply [lem-coef-accessible-full-inverse-image] with source and target both the locally presentable arrow category from Step 1, functor $T$ from Step 4, and replete accessible subcategory $\mathcal R$ from Step 2. This proves precisely the asserted replete accessibility, including generation by a small family and closure under sufficiently filtered colimits computed in the ambient arrow category. No abstract accessibility of $W$ alone is substituted for that conclusion.

source.place: Corollary A.2.6.8 proof, final paragraph, using Corollary A.2.6.7.

proof_origin.place: Expanded one-level split of Corollary A.2.6.8 (Smith), printed pp. 820-821, read online. The document is not archived in literature/; WANTED recorded in report.md.

The item statement is unchanged and agrees with A.2.6.8. It is not a target node, so no base-change morphism or coefficient category is involved. The split follows Lurie's proof. Step 1: the presheaf leaf with C=[1]^op and pullbacks from completeness gives a locally presentable M^[1]. Step 2: R=I^square=F∩W, using the item's generation hypothesis. Step 3: ^square F=C∩W is closed under retracts, pushouts, transfinite composites and isomorphisms, so i_f is a trivial cofibration. Step 4: T(f)=p_f is a functor and preserves κ-filtered colimits; this is genuinely elementary. Step 5: two-out-of-three gives W=T^{-1}R, and the inverse-image node applies with all hypotheses met. New nodes: both are true, self-contained, statement-only, and strictly smaller than the item. Small cases tested: I=∅, ∅→1 and 2→1 in Set; V=∅, V=D, H=id, H constant. Duplicates: full-inverse-image strictly generalizes arrow-inverse-image, which cannot be cited because T is not F^[1]. lean.statement: theorem model_weak_equivalences_accessible {M : Type u} [Category.{v} M] [ModelCategory M] [HasLimitsOfSize.{v, v} M] [HasColimitsOfSize.{v, v} M] [MorphismProperty.HasFunctorialFactorization (cofibrations M) (trivialFibrations M)] [MorphismProperty.HasFunctorialFactorization (trivialCofibrations M) (fibrations M)] [IsLocallyPresentable.{v} M] (I J : MorphismProperty M) [MorphismProperty.IsSmall.{v} I] [MorphismProperty.IsSmall.{v} J] (_hI : I.rlp = trivialFibrations M) (_hJ : J.rlp = fibrations M) : ObjectProperty.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms (fun f : Arrow M ↦ weakEquivalences M f.hom) ∧ ∃ (κ : Cardinal.{v}) (_ : Fact κ.IsRegular), (∀ (K : Type v) (_ : SmallCategory K) (_ : IsCardinalFiltered K κ) (D : K ⥤ Arrow M), (∀ k, weakEquivalences M (D.obj k).hom) → ∀ (c : Cocone D), Nonempty (IsColimit c) → weakEquivalences M c.pt.hom) ∧ ∃ (S : Type v) (G : S → Arrow M), (∀ s, weakEquivalences M (G s).hom) ∧ ∀ (f : Arrow M), weakEquivalences M f.hom → ∃ (K : Type v) (_ : SmallCategory K) (_ : IsCardinalFiltered K κ) (D : K ⥤ Arrow M) (c : Cocone D), (∀ k, ∃ s, Nonempty (D.obj k ≅ G s)) ∧ Nonempty (IsColimit c) ∧ Nonempty (c.pt ≅ f)
lean.note: The generating hypotheses are stated directly as small morphism properties with I.rlp = trivialFibrations M and J.rlp = fibrations M. The conclusion uses the explicit ambient-colimit and small-generation interface of the recorded accessibility proof dependencies. No simplicial enrichment, presentability of the conclusion generators, or fixed accessibility rank is assumed.
